2608.04980.title: Protoreasoning in Tiny Transformers
2608.04980.paper_summary: We show that tiny transformers can profitably employ a simple form of Chain of Thought, which we call protoreasoning, allowing us to study step-by-step reasoning on ~1M-parameter models and opening up opportunities for much more detailed experimentation and analysis than is feasible for larger models. Current Large Language Models exhibit impressive step-by-step reasoning, but we have yet to understand its generality, i.e., when and how LLMs learn genuinely general algorithms rather than "bags of heuristics." Such questions are hard to settle on compute-intensive frontier models trained on opaque data. To work at model scales far below the threshold for natural-language competence, we define reasoning-friendly tasks on Dyck languages (sentences of correctly nested brackets). We find that protoreasoning traces substantially close the out-of-distribution generalization gap, and ablations confirm that the trace's content, not merely its extra tokens, drives the gain.
2608.04980.paper_summary_zh: 我們展示了微小的Transformer可以有效地使用一種簡單的思維鏈形式，我們稱之為原始推理，這使我們能夠在約100萬參數的模型上進行逐步推理的研究，並開啟了比較大型模型更詳細的實驗和分析的機會。目前的大型語言模型展現了令人印象深刻的逐步推理能力，但我們尚未理解其普遍性，即大型語言模型何時以及如何學習真正通用的算法，而不是「啟發式的集合」。這些問題在計算密集的前沿模型上訓練於不透明數據時難以解決。為了在遠低於自然語言能力的模型規模上工作，我們在Dyck語言（正確嵌套括號的句子）上定義了有利於推理的任務。我們發現原始推理的痕跡實質上縮小了分佈外的泛化差距，並且消融實驗證實了痕跡的內容，而不僅僅是其額外的標記，驅動了增益。
2608.04980.author: Eduardo Valle et.al.
